About Melford

I've always been drawn to the moment where a pile of raw information turns into a decision someone can actually act on. Three years in financial crime operations at JPMorgan Chase in Mumbai is where that pull first showed up: learning to read transactions the way you'd read a room, noticing what's normal, what isn't, and why it matters. Before that, I traded derivatives intraday and co-founded Jumpstart Ventures, a small portfolio management venture, reading markets with that same instinct. Roles in customer service with Emirates Airlines and event operations with Divine Events & Hospitality taught me the other half: how operations actually run day to day, under pressure, in front of a real customer.

A Master of Business Informatics later, those two instincts finally had a name: analytics. It's the part of the job I enjoy most, taking something messy (a spreadsheet, a booking system, a set of transactions) and finding the story inside it that changes what someone does next. Working reservations at Abstract Hotel in Auckland keeps me close to that operational reality, while the six projects below are where I've put the analytics itself to work: forecasting, pricing, data warehousing, and the strategy to act on all of it.

01

Hotel Demand Forecasting Using Machine Learning

0.94AUC (in-era)
Predictive Analytics & Machine Learning

Stress-tested a top-performing demand model across a real market shift and exposed a 46% accuracy collapse that standard validation would have missed.

Compared four forecasting models trained on pre-pandemic hotel booking data and tested against post-pandemic bookings, to answer a question most model evaluations skip: does strong in-sample accuracy survive a real shift in market conditions?

  • Random Forest scored 0.9403 AUC within its training era but collapsed to 0.5124 (near-random) when evaluated cross-era, a 45.5% decline, showing how single-era validation can mask total unreliability under changed conditions.
  • SHAP analysis identified special requests and booking channel as the two strongest predictors of booking confirmation, jointly accounting for 41% of predictive influence.
  • Quantified the structural shift itself: a 74% compression in average booking lead time and a 17-percentage-point drop in confirmation rate between eras.
  • Delivered as a comprehensive research report and Power BI dashboard, with a six-stage governance framework for responsible deployment.
Pythonscikit-learn SHAPPower BIJupyter
02

City Hotel Business Intelligence & Data Warehouse

Business Intelligence & Data Warehousing

Built an end-to-end BI solution, from raw PMS exports to a live revenue and occupancy dashboard, for a 194-room hotel.

Built a complete BI solution end-to-end for an anonymised 194-room hotel: extracted raw PMS exports, cleaned and de-identified them in Python, and loaded them into a star-schema SQLite data warehouse feeding an interactive Power BI dashboard.

  • Designed the full ETL pipeline (extract, transform, load) handling PII removal, room-category standardisation, and stay-night calculation from raw arrival/departure logs.
  • Star-schema warehouse (10 fact/dimension tables) separates booking revenue, daily KPIs, and room inventory from date, room-category, market-segment, and booking-channel dimensions.
  • Dashboard surfaces Total Revenue, Occupancy, ADR, and RevPAR with drill-down by room category and channel, surfacing demand-driven pricing behaviour and premium-room revenue concentration.
PythonSQLite Power BIDAX
03

Hotel Demand & Dynamic Pricing Strategy

Demand Forecasting & Dynamic Pricing

Simulated a dynamic pricing strategy that redistributes revenue across demand periods without adding volatility or risk.

Used the public Hotel Booking Demand dataset (Kaggle) to forecast daily room-nights sold for a city hotel, then simulated a rule-based dynamic pricing strategy against a static-pricing baseline.

  • Regression-based demand model (calendar effects: month, weekend) achieved a Mean Absolute Error of 59.59 room-nights against a historical-average baseline, using a chronological, non-leaking train/test split.
  • Simulated dynamic pricing (discounting in low-demand periods, premium pricing in high-demand periods) matched the static-pricing baseline on total revenue while redistributing revenue across demand periods and smoothing utilisation without adding volatility.
  • Framed for a managerial audience: the value here isn't pure revenue maximisation, it's better price-demand alignment and more defensible pricing decisions.
Pythonpandas scikit-learnPower BI
04

SmartCare Health Monitoring

Predictive Health Analytics

Built a risk-classification model and dashboard that flags at-risk patients from wearable data, with privacy safeguards designed in from the start.

A preventive-care analytics case study for a health-monitoring provider: analysed continuous smartwatch data from 50 patients (age 50+) to identify hospitalisation risk before adverse events occur, under NZ's Privacy Act 2020 and Health Information Privacy Code.

  • Full pipeline: Python-based EDA and preprocessing, a logistic regression model classifying patients into risk categories, and a 4-page interactive Power BI dashboard with 10 custom DAX measures and cross-filtering slicers.
  • Connected physiological signals to actionable clinical triggers: patients sleeping under 6 hours for 3+ consecutive nights flagged for clinical review; 11 patients with heart-rate-max readings over 150 BPM flagged for cardiovascular referral.
  • Delivered a dedicated ethics section covering informed consent, data minimisation, and pseudonymisation, treating privacy as a design constraint, not an afterthought.

Dataset is synthetic, not real patient records.

The Warehouse Group: Big Data Integration Strategy

$3Mrevenue, 12mo
Enterprise Data Strategy

Analysed how a $3B retailer's data integration strategy delivered $3M in incremental revenue within 12 months.

A case study analysing how The Warehouse Group (New Zealand's largest non-food retailer, NZ$3B revenue, 260+ stores, 12,000+ employees) solved a real cross-brand data fragmentation problem using Adobe Experience Platform, Dynamic Yield, and Megaport.

  • Analysed how unifying eight previously siloed source systems (three websites, two mobile apps, three Salesforce instances) enabled 700+ unified customer segments and real-time personalisation at scale.
  • Connected the technology strategy to quantified outcomes: NZ$3M incremental revenue within 12 months, a 4.4% increase in revenue-per-user, a 26.4% click-through rate on personalised pages, and 400+ concurrent campaigns.
  • Assessed the initiative against an analytics-maturity framework (reaching "Prescriptive Analytics," the highest tier) with a structured risk assessment and six evidence-based recommendations for similar integrations.

06

Fonterra: Agricultural AI Innovation Strategy

AI Strategy & Innovation

Built a costed NZ$16M AI investment case for a NZ$22.9B dairy cooperative, projecting a 4.2x return.

A regulatory-compliance and AI adoption strategy for Fonterra Co-operative Group (NZ$22.9B FY2025 revenue, 140+ export markets, 10,000 shareholder farmers), built around stakeholder mapping, regulatory impact analysis, and a balanced scorecard for measuring outcomes.

  • Mapped ten stakeholder groups (regulators, farmer-shareholders, global buyers, investors, communities) by power and interest to identify where competing pressures for AI adoption converge.
  • Analysed the operational, financial, and governance impact of four regulatory forces (Food Act 2014, RMA/Zero Carbon Act, Animal Welfare Act, international standards including the EU AI Act) across six organisational dimensions.
  • Central argument: reframe regulation from a compliance cost into a strategic signal for exactly which data infrastructure to build, since it creates advantages global markets pay for.
  • Benchmarked Fonterra's AI capability (65/100) against global dairy majors Danone (75/100) and Nestle (82/100) using a VRIO framework, identifying its 20-year farmer dataset and IoT sensor network as the two genuinely inimitable competitive assets.
  • Recommendation package: a costed NZ$16M investment over 36 months, projecting a 4.2x return, a 30% emissions-intensity reduction by 2027, and cutting food-safety recall response time from days to under two hours.
Stakeholder AnalysisVRIO Framework Balanced Scorecard
